item.title: Republican Campaign Aide Is Fired Over Nazi Photo
item.author: Neil Vigdor and Tim Balk
item.content:encoded: Senator Jon Husted, running in a high-stakes race in Ohio, dismissed his political director because of social media activity displaying a “complete lack” of judgment, a spokeswoman said.

item.title: Trump Says He’d Love to See a ‘United’ Ireland During Visit
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump says he would like to see Ireland “unified,” a remark that puts him at odds with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham who recently said the issue is off the table. Olivia Fletcher reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Trump Is Wielding Power to Stifle Speech
item.author: Jim Rutenberg and Maggie Haberman
item.content:encoded: President Trump has harnessed agencies across the government to curtail press freedoms, a sweeping campaign that free speech advocates say will have lasting effects.

item.title: Republican Groups Rush to Paxton’s Aid in Texas After Staying on Sidelines
item.author: Theodore Schleifer
item.content:encoded: An organization allied with Senate G.O.P. leaders has booked more than $51 million in ads. Now, Ken Paxton has a financial edge after months of being outspent by his Democratic rival.

item.title: Trump’s Convention Promises Face Tough Road Even If GOP Wins
item.author: Erik Wasson, Caitlin Reilly and Ari Natter
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump and top Republicans made several concrete policy promises during their Dallas midterm convention, but they all face massive headwinds in Congress even if the GOP retains control of both chambers.

item.title: Trump Wades Into Debate Over Irish Unification
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump stirred debate during his visit to Dublin by saying he would like to see a united Ireland and that unification is eventually inevitable, departing from the caution US presidents have traditionally shown on the issue. Bloomberg News White House Reporter Jennifer Dlouhy tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that the remarks drew support from Sinn Féin and criticism from unionists, while UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there is currently no mandate for a referendum. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Farage’s Reform Raises Record £72 Million in Less Than 24 Hours
item.author: Jillian Deutsch and Alex Morales
item.content:encoded: Nigel Farage’s Reform UK received a second multi-million pound donation, bringing the total raised over the past 24 hours to £72 million ($97 million) and far surpassing the amounts raised by the rival Labour and Conservative parties so far this year.

item.title: BRICS Countries Call for Maximum Restraint in the Middle East
item.author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen
item.content:encoded: BRICS nations including Iran and the United Arab Emirates have expressed “deep concern” over escalating tensions in the Middle East, using a joint statement published on Saturday to call for “maximum restraint” in the region.

item.title: Iraq Fires Commander After Drone Attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline
item.author: Khalid Al-Ansary and Devika Krishna Kumar
item.content:encoded: Iraq is moving to contain the fallout from attacks that caused the closure of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, after the strikes were found to have been launched from inside the country.

item.title: Trump Sees Canada Deal ‘Fairly Soon,’ Downplays Leaving USMCA
